title: Vikarna speaks for her
hook: Bhima answers with fire, Arjuna holds him back, and Vikarna, a Kaurava, answers with reasons
carry: dharma comes before your own side
tomorrow: What happens when they pull at her sari?

segments.voice: Yesterday Draupadi's question met Bhishma's silence. In the story families tell, the food he lived on had clouded him. As the food, so the mind.

Two voices break the silence, and they break it in opposite directions. First Bhima. He has watched his eldest brother stake him, lose him, and then lose Draupadi, and his anger has nowhere to go. In the telling, he turns it on Yudhishthira himself. Then someone nobody expects speaks up, a young man from the other side of the family. Two answers to Draupadi's question: one made of fury, one made of reasons.
screen: `TWO VOICES BREAK THE SILENCE.` → `ONE WITH FURY.` → `ONE WITH REASONS.`

segments.voice: Bhima's words are shocking. Gamblers, he says, don't stake even the women kept in their houses. Then: Sahadeva, bring fire, and I'll burn this brother's arms. It's the rage of someone who loves his brother and can't bear what he's done. Arjuna stops him: our enemies want exactly this, to see us turn on our eldest. And Bhima holds back. Then Vikarna speaks. He's one of Duryodhana's own brothers, a Kaurava, and he stands up in his family's hall and says: answer her. Nobody does. So he answers it himself, with reasons. Kings, he says, are prone to certain vices: hunting, drinking, dice, and too much pleasure. A man in their grip acts without judgment. Yudhishthira staked Draupadi in the grip of the game, at Shakuni's prompting, after he had already lost himself. And she's the wife of all five brothers, not his alone. For these reasons, Vikarna says, she was not won. The hall erupts, cheering him and blaming Shakuni. Notice who gave the answer: not an elder, not a Pandava, but a younger brother of the winning side. That's a real Hindu teaching, and the epics keep coming back to it. Dharma isn't loyalty to your own team. It binds you even against your own family. The tradition honors the ones who said so: Vikarna here, and in the Ramayana, Vibhishana, who told his own brother Ravana to give Sita back. And see how Vikarna does it: not with Bhima's fire, but with reasons, out loud, in his own family's hall.
screen: `BHIMA: BRING FIRE.` · `VIKARNA, A KAURAVA, STANDS UP.` · `HIS REASONS: SHE WAS NOT WON.` · `NOT AN ELDER, NOT A PANDAVA.` · then, large: `DHARMA BEFORE YOUR OWN SIDE.`

segments.voice: Think of a place where you belong to a side: a family, a team, a friend group. Is there one true thing your side would rather nobody said? Don't say it yet. Shape it the way Vikarna did, a reason instead of a shout. Many Hindus make a sankalpa, a small resolve, before their home shrine. If you pray, make yours there and ask for courage; if you don't, write the sentence down and keep it.
Draupadi's question. Bhima answers with fire, Arjuna holds him back, and Vikarna, a Kaurava, answers with reasons: she was not won.
Your line: dharma comes before your own side. Vikarna said it in his own family's hall. Day seven hundred seventy-two, done.

howItsDone: Vikarna is remembered in retellings as the Kaurava who spoke for Draupadi, held up beside Vibhishana as one who put dharma before his own side; Arjuna's restraint of Bhima is told as the brothers refusing to turn on each other.

Vikarna.meaning: a brother of Duryodhana who speaks up for Draupadi

Kaurava.meaning: a son of Dhritarashtra, on Duryodhana's side of the family

Sahadeva.meaning: the youngest of the five Pandava brothers

Arjuna.meaning: the third Pandava brother, a great archer

Vibhishana.meaning: Ravana's brother, who urged him to return Sita and left him for Rama

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Dyuta Parva (Bhima's anger at Yudhishthira and call for fire; Arjuna's restraint; Vikarna's speech on the four vices of kings, the order of the stakes and Draupadi as wife of all five; the assembly's applause)
Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Vibhishana counsels Ravana to return Sita, is rejected, and goes over to Rama)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm Bhima's words (gamblers do not stake even their serving women; 'Sahadeva, bring fire, I will burn his arms/hands').
